newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKCB Bank to gain from CRE stake-analysts.
newsitem.headline: HKCB Bank to gain from CRE stake-analysts.

text.p: HKCB Bank Holdings Ltd is expected to benefit from new growth opportunities brought about by the change in its shareholding structure, analysts said.
China Resources Enterprises Ltd (CRE) said on Thursday it acquired 50 percent of Hongkong Chinese Bank Ltd and injected it into a new joint-venture company set up with Lippo Ltd.

CRE and Lippo will have equal stakes in the joint-venture company, Lippo CRE Financial Services Ltd. The company in turn will hold 74.4 percent of HKCB Bank Holding Co Ltd, with the remaining 25.6 percent held by the public.
"China Resources (Enterprises) will become more active in its dealing with HKCB," said Steven Thompson, analyst at Nikko Securities.
HKCB Holdings will hold 100 percent of the company's main asset, Hongkong Chinese Bank.
"The bank will benefit from the greater transparency a wholly public rather than private shareholding structure brings it," one Hong Kong analyst said.

A more transparent operation with clear reporting lines should help boost the bank's credit rating. A higher credit rating would help the bank obtain money at lower interest rates, which would increase profit margins, he said.
The deal is believed to be the strategy of CRE managing director Frank Ning.
Lippo Ltd, which held 59.3 percent of HKCB Bank Holding before the deal, has yet to release a statement on the transaction.
The change in the shareholding structure will raise HKCB Bank Holding's asset base by approximately HK$2 billion, not the equity base of Hongkong Chinese Bank.
"CRE is not planning to increase the capital base of the bank at this time," said a source close to the deal.
Under a shareholders' agreement between CRE and Lippo, the Lippo group will continue to control HKCB Holding and Hongkong Chinese Bank.
But with the bank 100 percent owned by one company, the decision-making process should be smoother and allow the banks to grow faster whether through equity or debt issues, the analyst said.

China Resources Enterprises has been publicly listed since 1992. Its parent company China Resources (Holdings) is a state-owned trading conglomerate controlled by the Ministry of Foreign Economic Relations and Trade (Moftec). It has total assets of US$28 billion, located mostly in Hong Kong.
